subject: QuietHour Tech - request for nighttime isolation / dedicated pool amendment
body:
From: Maya Lopez <m.lopez@quiethour-tech.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: nighttime isolation for dedicated GPUs (quiet hours)

Hi Naomi,

Quick one — we operate a nightly batch window that runs between 02:00–05:00 PDT and it spikes our token throughput by ~8x. Our current dedicated pool is great during the day but we saw tail latency spikes from noisy tenants last week during a maintenance-induced rebalancing. For regulatory reasons we need stronger guarantees for that window (both lower tail latency and a hard throughput floor).

Can Redwood provide an addendum that:
- reserves a soft-isolated lane for our pool during 02:00–05:00 PDT (not full node carveout, but isolation that prevents tenant preemption),
- guarantees a minimum inflight token throughput of 120k tokens/min for that window (we can trade some daytime credits), and
- documents fallback behavior and observability we can use in our runbook?

If you can send a proposed wording and any technical constraints, I’ll loop in Legal. We’re on a June billing cycle so hope to land this quickly.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Lopez
Ops Lead, QuietHour Tech
[Attachment: nightly_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: nighttime isolation for dedicated GPUs (quiet hours)

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask and the snapshot. I’m putting Ben (account) and Steph (runtime infra) on this thread so we can propose both contractual language and the engineering pattern.

Ben — can you scope whether this is a pricing/credit trade or if we need a different SKU?
Steph — high level: is a priority lane + reserved tokens approach feasible for that 3-hour window, or do we have to do time-sliced node reservations? Any observability gaps to call out?

I’ll combine the inputs into a short amendment draft for QuietHour Legal.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Lopez <m.lopez@quiethour-tech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: nighttime isolation for dedicated GPUs (quiet hours)

Thanks Naomi / Maya. Quick commercial note — we can structure this two ways:

1) Time-sliced reservation (we allocate a soft-fraction of reserved capacity for the 02:00–05:00 window). That gives the cleanest economic guarantee but requires a commit amendment (monthly reserve credits shifted to night window).

2) Priority-lane + guaranteed inflight tokens for the window (lower upfront contract changes). That would be a managed SLO: we provide >=120k tokens/min for the window, backed by operational credits if missed.

Given QuietHour’s billing timeline, option 2 gets you live faster. Commercially we’d offset by increasing daytime usage discounts or by a small monthly uplift (I’ll put numbers in the proposal doc). Lauren — can you pull the current commit and propose the uplift matrix?

Maya — I’ll attach a short amendment draft (contract framing) with both options and clear handoffs for alerts/escalation. Naomi — please let us know if QuietHour prefers a contractual floor vs operational credit approach.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reserved_gpu_amendment_v1.pdf (PDF, 68KB)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Lopez <m.lopez@quiethour-tech.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2026 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: nighttime isolation for dedicated GPUs (quiet hours)

Hi all — technical context and constraints from Infra/Runtime: we have two pragmatic approaches. I’ll summarize pros/cons and include the minimal observability we must add.

A) Priority lane + guaranteed inflight tokens (recommended as Option 2):
- Implementation: create a tenant-priority queue with token-bucket enforcement during the 02:00–05:00 window. Requests from QuietHour get priority tag; the runtime reserves N tokens/sec for that tag.
- Guarantees: we can set a guaranteed inflight floor that maps to the 120k tokens/min. If we hit a shortfall (hardware failure or contention), the control plane will trigger the fallback (automated model-variant routing or temporary soft-capacity borrow from a cold pool).
- Observability: need token-level counters, per-tenant latency histograms for the window, and an SLO alert rule. Currently we have most of these metrics but not the short-window percentile histograms (we’ll add them).
- Limitations: this is not absolute physical isolation — extreme failure modes (node-level outage) can still impact the guarantee. For absolute isolation we need time-sliced node reservations which require more lead time.

B) Time-sliced node reservation (Option 1):
- True isolation during the window but requires orchestrator changes and billing commit amendment. Lead time: ~3 weeks to schedule and test for your fleet size.

Proposed next engineering steps:
1. We’ll instrument the 02:00–05:00 window with per-tenant p50/p95/p99 histograms (estimated 2 business days).
2. Build the priority-lane token-bucket control (target: 7 business days for rollout to staging, 14 days to prod).
3. Run a 3-night canary with QuietHour traffic shape and validate fallbacks.

I attached a short runbook and the minimal metric definitions you’ll see.

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal SRE, Runtime — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: quiethour_draft_runbook.md (MD, 6KB)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Lopez <m.lopez@quiethour-tech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, QuietHour Tech Legal <legal@quiethour-tech.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: nighttime isolation for dedicated GPUs (quiet hours)

Maya — thanks for the details and for being flexible on approach. Summary / proposed path forward: 

- We recommend Option 2 (priority lane + guaranteed inflight tokens) as the fastest path. Engineering estimates: metrics instrumentation 2 business days, priority-lane rollout to staging within 7 business days, production after a 3-night canary (14 business days total).
- Commercial framing: Ben will provide an amendment that includes the 120k tokens/min SLO for 02:00–05:00 PDT, with operational credits if the SLO is missed. If QuietHour instead prefers hard node carveouts, we can do a time-sliced reservation but it will require a commit change and ~3 weeks lead time.
- Deliverables we will circulate: (a) a one-page amendment with both options for signature, (b) an engineering runbook and metric dashboard, (c) a 3-night canary schedule. I attached the draft amendment and runbook for review.

Next steps: 
1) Maya / QuietHour Legal: please review the attached amendment (reserved_gpu_amendment_v1.pdf) and the runbook. If the amendment wording looks ok, we can route to DocuSign and target signature next week.
2) Ben / Lauren: send the commercial uplift matrix and new PRICING line item.
3) Steph: please start instrumentation and ping QuietHour with canary dates.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to go line-by-line.

Thanks all,
—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
